units.spine: The market sits on the busiest way through the village, and a stranger who keeps to that way arrives at the stalls without asking anyone.
Safety here is somebody's trade and not a matter of luck and good neighbours. The charter hall and the veterans' lodge are as ordinary in the village as the mill.
Money is not short here, and what people argue about instead is their own business.
What Hochhausen needs it can get, and what it makes it can move.
The village could stand a first push and not a second.
The people of the village count themselves a match for the trouble they know, and say nothing about the other kind.
Nothing here is organised against what lives beyond the fields, and each household answers for its own fences.
Disputes are opened here more readily than they are settled.
A rider who stopped a night says the place has nothing spare for anyone passing through.
No one here works magic, nothing is arranged with anyone who does, and nobody expects that to change.
Hunger here would come out of the fields and never off the road.
A day in the village shows nothing of the quarrel between The Commercial Circle and The Administrative Circle, though it is no secret to anyone who stays.
Goods come into the village and goods go out of it, and nobody here remarks on either.
The road is what the village lives by, and people come along it as steadily as goods.
Hochhausen has grown to the size a village of its kind grows to, and stopped there.
One of the village's ties weighs more than the rest, and the weight of it shows in what the place agrees to and what it does not.
Households here are tied to one another as they are in any settled place, and nothing in that is particular to this one.
A single loose end runs through the village, and it is the kind that one institution would tie off.
